Title: Agree the pilot scope and observable success criteria
User story: As a product owner, I want a short decision sheet and reviewed operator flows, so the team builds the agreed Instagram MVP and can accept each increment.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The sheet identifies pilot accounts, owners, source modes, formats, brand inputs, limits and decisions still awaiting evidence.
2. Thresholds and operating numbers are explicitly proposed or accepted; none are misrepresented as PRD requirements.
3. An intended operator can walk through draft correction, calendar actions and pause/resume using a small Persian prototype.
Demo: Walk through the decision sheet and three Persian operator flows; identify each open decision and owner.
Blocker: Pending account and named-owner identity, source/brand/calendar inputs, and intended-operator review; recommended defaults selected.

Title: Prove that the pilot Instagram account supports the required operations
User story: As a product owner, I want an evidence-backed platform capability matrix, so platform restrictions are visible before connector implementation.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Selected login flow, API version, account type, permissions, approval steps and credential lifecycle are recorded.
2. Authorized tests provide evidence for core publishing formats and available post/Story metrics; carousel and disclosure capabilities are also checked.
3. Missing access has a named blocker and resolution owner; a mocked success cannot close an unavailable capability.
Demo: Show redacted authorized platform results and one permission/capability blocker with its resolution path.
Blocker: US-001 remains in progress; pilot account and authorized Meta app/test access are not identified, so account-specific probes remain outstanding.

Title: Prove access to company data and approved trend inputs
User story: As a editorial owner, I want representative source samples and access contracts, so content research starts from data we can actually retrieve and cite.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A representative company feed can be read with source identity, dates, status and eligibility fields.
2. Approved industry sources, search/social signals and sector-account inputs have permitted retrieval paths or explicit blockers.
3. Samples retain original links and collection times; private or unavailable sources are not assumed accessible.
Demo: Show normalized company and trend samples next to their original sources and eligibility fields.
Blocker: US-001 remains in progress; company feed, approved source list, permitted access paths, and genuine samples are not supplied.

Title: Select a workable Persian model and rendering approach
User story: As a editorial owner, I want a reproducible Persian quality and cost benchmark, so chosen models and templates can produce usable content at a known pilot cost.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The fixed examples cover claims, register, glossary, ZWNJ, mixed-script RTL, digit/calendar preferences and actual rendered text.
2. Writer and independent reviewer roles are evaluated separately; model/prompt versions, failures, latency and cost per accepted asset are recorded.
3. A source-data chart and short caption-led video render correctly; speech and generated-clip options have explicit enable/disable decisions.
Demo: Show one accepted and one rejected Persian example, the actual chart/video render, and cost/version results.

Title: Run the whole project locally from a fresh checkout
User story: As a developer, I want a Dockerized backend/frontend monorepo with a passing build, so any team member can reproduce the same starting environment.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Documented bootstrap starts /backend, /frontend, PostgreSQL, Redis, workers and one scheduler without host Python/Node.
2. A frontend request reaches Django/DRF; resolved supported dependencies are locked and development reload works.
3. Database/media persist through restart; default sample providers cannot publish externally; basic containerized CI is green.
Demo: Start from a fresh checkout, open the frontend/API, restart the stack and show persisted sample data.
Blocker: US-001 acceptance/operator review remains pending; Docker/Compose is not installed here, so image build, fresh bootstrap, and restart validation are pending.

Title: Receive consistent Persian errors from the API and dashboard
User story: As a operator, I want clear validation and failure messages with a support reference, so I can recover without deciphering raw technical errors.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The API has versioned routes, bounded pagination, permission defaults, OpenAPI and the central machine-code/Persian-message contract.
2. Nested validation, CSRF/auth denial, stale edit, throttle, provider timeout and unexpected failure produce documented safe responses.
3. The shared frontend client renders field/global errors, retains request IDs and retries only when the operation is safe.
Demo: Submit an invalid form, trigger a safe fixture failure and show the Persian message, field paths and matching request ID.
Evidence: backend/apps/core/errors.py; backend/apps/core/middleware.py; backend/apps/core/pagination.py; docs/openapi.yaml; frontend/src/lib/api.ts; frontend/src/App.tsx; frontend/src/main.tsx
Blocker: US-005 remains in progress; container/runtime/browser acceptance evidence for this story is pending. Docker/Compose, Django/DRF and npm are unavailable here.

Title: Sign in and navigate the Persian RTL dashboard
User story: As a staff member, I want a secure Persian dashboard showing my role and current account context, so I can reach operational tools with clear navigation.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Admin-created staff can log in/out with protected sessions and CSRF; disabled staff cannot continue privileged access.
2. Admin and operations permissions are enforced at the API, including direct requests; there is no public signup.
3. The right-side navigation, font, dialogs, forms, focus order and mixed Persian/Latin text work on wide and narrow screens.
Demo: Sign in as operations and admin, switch account context and prove direct API denial of an admin action.

Title: Trace a failed action and inspect its audit history
User story: As a admin, I want correlated errors, health and an audit view, so I can explain what happened without exposing credentials or content in logs.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A frontend/API/worker failure is traceable by request/run ID, release and environment in the selected tracker and structured logs.
2. Account/rule/control actions produce read-only audit events with actor, time, target and reason.
3. Health shows dependency readiness; logs/tracker redact secrets and sensitive outputs, and tracker outage does not block the application.
Demo: Trigger a worker fixture failure, follow its run/request ID and show a redacted audit event in the dashboard.

Title: Connect an Instagram account and see whether it is ready
User story: As a admin, I want secure connection settings and account health, so I can identify missing access before attempting production.
Acceptance criteria:
1. An admin can configure/test/reconnect the chosen integration and rotate its secret reference; operations cannot access credential controls.
2. Account setup lists required missing capabilities, token health and shadow mode; raw credentials never appear in ordinary reads/logs/exports.
3. Expiry/revocation produces an actionable connection state and a documented refresh/recovery path.
Demo: Connect/test an authorized account, show shadow readiness, then simulate expiry and its recovery instructions.

Title: Configure the brand and Persian presentation preferences
User story: As a admin, I want a saved brand kit and editorial preferences for an account, so generated content uses our identity and language conventions.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Logo/colors/font, tone/register, approved glossary, digit style, calendar and timezone can be saved and previewed.
2. Uploaded brand assets have type/size validation, origin and rights metadata; missing/expired rights make an asset unusable.
3. Persian/Latin digits, Latin handles, Jalali/Gregorian boundaries and timezone conversion are covered by fixed examples; changes create an audited rule version.
Demo: Change tone, brand and calendar/digits, preview the result and reject an asset with expired rights.

Title: Configure sourcing, posting and automation rules
User story: As a admin, I want validated account rules with visible limits, so production follows an explicit plan instead of hidden defaults.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Source mode, eligibility, permitted formats, posting slots/limits, sensitive topics and check thresholds are editable.
2. Retry/correction, budget, shadow and experiment thresholds have explicit units and accepted defaults; invalid combinations cannot save.
3. Rule changes create audit/version records and mark affected unpublished checks stale; incomplete accounts remain visibly unready.
Demo: Save a valid rule set, reject an invalid one and show the new version plus invalidated unpublished checks.

Title: Choose approved models and safely change their prompts
User story: As a admin, I want role-specific model and fallback settings with a regression gate, so I can improve providers without silently reducing Persian quality.
Acceptance criteria:
1. All 13 PRD roles have provider/model/version/prompt configuration and an explicit evaluated fallback where configured.
2. Writer and Persian reviewer run independently; an unchanged provider may serve several roles without merging their contracts.
3. A failing fixed regression set prevents promotion; accepted changes are versioned, audited and invalidate dependent results.
Demo: Reject a bad prompt promotion; accept a passing version and show independent writer/reviewer configuration.

Title: Run one production stage and inspect its durable result
User story: As a operator, I want a visible stage run that survives retries and process restarts, so I can tell whether work is running, completed or needs attention.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A requested stage returns an asynchronous run ID and persists validated inputs/outputs, versions, latency, usage and outcome.
2. Malformed model output cannot advance the pipeline; duplicate delivery or a worker crash does not create conflicting successful results.
3. The dashboard displays running/succeeded/held/failed detail and links to a safe error reason and audit/run history. This increment uses fixture providers; paid production calls stay disabled until US-014 budget controls are accepted.
Demo: Run a sample stage, inspect its result, kill/restart the worker and prove safe duplicate-delivery recovery.

Title: Keep paid runs and recovery inside account budgets
User story: As a admin, I want enforced cost/seconds caps and bounded retry behavior, so failures and concurrent jobs cannot create uncontrolled spending.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Paid calls reserve bounded cost before execution across draft/account/month scopes; actual costs and generated seconds are recorded.
2. Concurrent jobs cannot reserve past a cap; ambiguous paid responses retain reservations pending reconciliation.
3. Safe transient retry, approved fallback and correction-loop limits survive restart; exhausted work holds with an alertable reason.
Demo: Launch concurrent fixture jobs at the spending cap and show one held reservation plus a bounded retry outcome.

Title: Browse eligible company-feed candidates and their original sources
User story: As a operator, I want a refreshed candidate list with eligibility reasons, so I can see which company items can enter production and why.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Configured feed ingestion runs on schedule with freshness/status/exclusion filtering and retained source IDs/links/timestamps.
2. Replay and pagination do not duplicate candidates; failed feeds show stale/error state without blocking other accounts.
3. The Persian research screen exposes eligible/excluded examples and safe source fetching cannot reach disallowed internal addresses.
Demo: Refresh a representative feed twice and show the same candidate set with inclusion/exclusion reasons.

Title: Verify claims and build a reproducible chart dataset
User story: As a operator, I want source-linked claims and calculations for a selected candidate, so every number used in content can be explained and reproduced.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Figures, units, dates and textual claims retain an original-source locator and evidence status.
2. Comparisons and percentage changes run in deterministic code; chart-ready values retain their inputs and calculation version.
3. Unsupported or conflicting figures are excluded and block dependent content; evidence and conflicts are visible in the dashboard.
Demo: Reproduce a chart calculation from source values and show that a contradictory figure blocks dependent content.

Title: Generate a Persian brief, caption and scene plan
User story: As a operator, I want editable Persian copy and a structured plan from verified information, so the writer and visual stages work from the same approved facts.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A selected eligible candidate produces a versioned brief, angle/format, hook, script, caption, overlays and cover copy.
2. Storyboard, timed scenes, shot list and asset plan reference the same brief and verified claims.
3. Outputs respect tone/glossary/digit/calendar settings and the allowed format; failed or unsupported structured output stays held.
Demo: Generate one Persian brief/caption/storyboard and follow a scene claim back to the original evidence.

Title: Render a source-driven Persian infographic for a feed post
User story: As a operator, I want an actual branded single-image preview generated from the dataset, so I can judge the first complete media output.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A versioned template renders chart values directly from the verified dataset with readable Persian text and brand settings.
2. Output and preview have persisted hashes/storage keys and source/rights/disclosure metadata.
3. Missing/expired input rights or unmet disclosure requirements hold the draft; the preview reflects the actual stored render.
Demo: Open the stored branded infographic beside its dataset and show a rights/disclosure failure staying held.

Title: Upload media or edit a draft without losing revision safety
User story: As a operator, I want bounded copy/media edits and a clear preview, so I can correct content while the system knows what must be checked again.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Supported uploads and editable copy/overlay/cover fields save as a new immutable revision with safe size/type checks.
2. Stale edits return a conflict; unsaved changes and recoverable failures preserve input and show useful feedback.
3. Changed dependencies mark old outputs/checks stale; old scheduled revision references cannot be silently published.
Demo: Edit copy in two sessions, show the stale-write conflict, and verify that the changed revision requires new checks.

Title: See independent quality checks and understand why an image is held
User story: As a operator, I want an explainable pass/fail/uncertain result for every required check, so only evidence-backed, usable Persian content becomes ready.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Evidence, Persian language, brand, media, rights/disclosure and platform checks record score/reason/current revision and affected inputs.
2. The Persian reviewer runs separately from the writer and checks actual text/render examples, including glossary, ZWNJ, register and digit/calendar rules.
3. Only current all-pass results at account thresholds produce readiness; uncertain, sensitive, stale or hard-failed content holds with a clear explanation.
Demo: Compare passed, failed and uncertain examples and explain why only one becomes ready.

Title: Fill a shadow calendar with checked single-image content
User story: As a operator, I want automatically planned image slots and a usable calendar, so I can inspect the first source-to-schedule workflow before any automatic publishing.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Account rules create unique timezone-aware slots and select eligible nonrepeating company candidates for the enabled image format.
2. Only the current all-pass revision is scheduled; unsuitable or late content leaves an open/held slot with a readable reason.
3. Calendar week/list views show account timezone and calendar preference; shadow mode issues zero publish calls.
Demo: Let a sample feed fill a shadow slot, inspect calendar details and prove that no publish call was issued.

Title: Pause, reschedule or cancel work safely
User story: As a operator or admin, I want clear calendar actions and visible global/account stop controls, so the team can control pending work without accidental restart.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Operations can reschedule/cancel permitted work; only admins use global/account kill switches.
2. Pause moves pending scheduled items to held and blocks future dispatch authorization; cancellation/stale edits are respected by queued work.
3. Resume shows consequences and requires explicit eligible rescheduling/rechecks; audit records include scope/actor/reason, and remote in-flight limitations are explained.
Demo: Pause an account, show scheduled items held, reschedule one eligible item and prove resume alone sends nothing.

Title: Resolve an exception or download the content for manual handling
User story: As a operator, I want an actionable queue, bounded recovery and a complete export, so routine failures can be handled without database or shell access.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Held/failed items show their real cause, affected stage/check and safe recovery action with remaining retry/budget limits.
2. Authorized export contains media/copy and evidence/rights/check manifest, with no secrets; unusable content remains clearly marked.
3. The chosen transport delivers deduplicated hold/failure/budget alerts with dashboard links; recovery is audited and alert-delivery failure is visible.
Demo: Open a held item from an alert, inspect the reason and download the authorized media/copy/evidence export.

Title: Correct only the affected scene and reuse valid work
User story: As a operator, I want targeted correction with visible reuse, so a small change does not regenerate already accepted assets.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Checks can identify scene/claim targets and launch a bounded targeted correction for a new revision.
2. Dependency fingerprints include upstream data, model/prompt/rule/template versions; valid unaffected asset hashes remain unchanged.
3. Changed outputs and dependent checks rerun before readiness; exhausted correction becomes held with a specific reason.
Demo: Flag one scene, rerun it and compare stored hashes showing untouched scenes were reused.

Title: Collect approved industry, search and sector-account signals
User story: As a operator, I want scheduled trend-source updates with supporting links, so research covers the approved sources in addition to company feeds.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The approved source set covers industry sources, search/social signals and sector accounts through permitted supported access.
2. Each signal retains origin, identity/link and source/fetch times; source failures and stale collections are visible and isolated.
3. Source allowlists and safe fetching apply; missing required access stays an explicit blocker rather than becoming fabricated data.
Demo: Show fresh linked signals from each approved input category and a failed source isolated from healthy ones.

Title: Choose ranked, relevant trend topics for upcoming slots
User story: As a operator, I want explainable topic ranking and automatic nonrepeating selection, so the calendar uses timely relevant topics when evidence is sufficient.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Related signals form topics with retained original links and deterministic component scores for freshness, relevance, audience fit and evidence.
2. Company/trend/combined modes follow agreed rules, coverage history and repeat avoidance; ranked eligible topics enter the existing verified production flow.
3. No eligible topic means an open slot; scores and exclusion reasons are inspectable without invented claims or reactions.
Demo: Inspect a ranked topic and score breakdown, then show that repeated/weak topics leave a slot open.

Title: Produce a caption-led Reel from owned footage
User story: As a operator, I want a complete Persian Reel preview with timed scenes and captions, so video production works using reusable assets and bounded rendering.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The shared brief yields timed video scenes, footage/asset choices, caption/overlay/cover copy and a valid assembled Reel.
2. Persian text, subtitle timing, clipping, continuity, brand and format checks run on the actual rendered output.
3. Flagging one real video scene rerenders only that scene and dependent assembly/checks; preview and crop reflect current stored media.
Demo: Play the actual Persian Reel, flag one real scene and show only the relevant outputs/checks changing.

Title: Turn verified figures into an animated chart
User story: As a operator, I want a Persian chart animation driven by the saved dataset, so numerical content stays reproducible throughout video production.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Animated values, labels, units and comparisons come directly from the versioned dataset, with readable Persian text.
2. The template respects brand/safe areas and reuses the video assembly/check/preview workflow.
3. Changing a dataset value invalidates its chart scenes and dependent checks while unrelated scenes remain reusable.
Demo: Play the chart animation next to the numeric dataset and change one input to demonstrate correct invalidation.

Title: Produce a short template-based motion explainer
User story: As a operator, I want a coherent Persian motion-graphics explanation, so verified ideas can be presented without new footage for every scene.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A structured storyboard produces a short branded explainer with timed graphics, transitions and readable Persian overlays.
2. Claims remain linked to the brief/evidence and only rights-cleared assets are used.
3. Scene edits reuse valid assets and the same Persian/media/platform checks gate readiness.
Demo: Play a complete motion explainer and inspect its structured scenes and source-linked claims.

Title: Prepare an image Story with an accurate crop preview
User story: As a operator, I want a checked Persian image Story, so the same research and production pipeline supports the Story image format.
Acceptance criteria:
1. An existing verified topic/dataset or permitted uploaded image can produce an image Story using account rules.
2. Actual crop/safe-area preview and current platform/image/Persian/rights checks cover the final asset.
3. Story slots appear in the calendar; unsupported options are explained and shadow still makes zero publish calls.
Demo: Preview generated and uploaded image Stories with safe-area/crop warnings and readiness states.

Title: Prepare a caption-led video Story
User story: As a operator, I want a checked Persian video Story, so all priority formats can pass through the shadow workflow.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A verified brief or permitted video upload produces a valid video Story with readable timed captions.
2. Format-specific duration/codec/crop/timing checks and current independent quality/rights checks are retained.
3. A video-Story scene correction preserves unaffected work and the calendar accurately shows its readiness/hold state.
Demo: Play a checked video Story, inspect subtitle timing and correct one scene without rebuilding valid scenes.

Title: Keep optional narration and generated clips under explicit controls
User story: As a admin, I want an evaluated enablement boundary for optional paid media, so caption-led production remains usable and optional generation stays safe and bounded.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Caption-led output works with speech/clip providers disabled; unsupported optional controls are visibly unavailable.
2. If narration is enabled, approved voice, pronunciation/alignment review and a usable caption-led alternative are demonstrated.
3. If generated clips are enabled, origin/rights/disclosure and seconds/cost caps are enforced; disabled adapters cannot be invoked by a source or model.
Demo: Render with optional services disabled; for any enabled option demonstrate its actual cap and quality/rights checks.
Release gate: Core controls; optional provider implementation only if enabled

Title: Audit a native Persian sample and operate all core formats in shadow
User story: As a editorial reviewer, I want a recorded quality sample and manual-publication references, so we can judge production/check accuracy before enabling autonomy.
Acceptance criteria:
1. All four priority formats run through research, production, checks and the calendar in shadow; no automatic publish call occurs.
2. A native reviewer records sampled findings and agreement with check decisions; critical findings return affected work to held and regression examples.
3. Staff can export/manual-publish permitted output and record the resulting platform ID/reference; audit cadence and shadow evidence are visible.
Demo: Review all priority formats in shadow, record native audit results and attach a manual-publication reference.

Title: Use a secure hosted pilot environment with traceable releases
User story: As a operator, I want a deployed protected dashboard and bounded worker stack, so the team can use the MVP outside developer machines.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A release-tagged frontend/API/worker stack serves HTTPS on one origin with secrets injection, one scheduler and bounded resource/concurrency settings.
2. Session/CSRF/role, private-media/export, upload and source-fetch boundaries pass hosted checks; untrusted source text cannot alter tools/rules.
3. The deployment/migration procedure records image/config versions and rollback boundaries; CI includes the implemented critical browser journeys.
Demo: Use the hosted release as operations/admin, follow a correlated failure and inspect the release/security evidence.

Title: Restore pilot data and clean up only records past retention
User story: As a operations owner, I want a proven restore and conservative retention process, so we can recover and keep only the agreed history.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Database, media, configuration and secret-reference/access recovery are documented and a representative isolated restore succeeds.
2. Scheduled backups are monitored and the proposed recovery targets are measured against the chosen environment.
3. Retention cleanup follows approved periods and preserves active tests, required published/audit/check evidence and rights dependencies.
Demo: Restore an isolated backup, open a recovered draft/asset and preview retention selections before cleanup.

Title: Prepare publish-ready media containers without sending a post
User story: As a admin, I want inspectable Instagram preparation results for each core format, so the connector can be validated before automated dispatch is permitted.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The version-pinned adapter validates capability, credential and quota state and prepares containers/readiness for authorized test media.
2. Recorded container IDs are reused safely; expiring media URLs remain reachable for provider ingestion without exposing unrelated media.
3. The preparation flow never publishes a post, and unsupported options, expiry or provider errors map into the existing exception contract.
Demo: Prepare core media containers, inspect recorded readiness and prove no publish call has occurred.

Title: Publish one due single-image item safely on an authorized test account
User story: As a admin, I want one guarded, recoverable automatic single-image send, so the first external side effect has complete duplicate and uncertainty protection.
Acceptance criteria:
1. A due checked single-image revision on an explicitly authorized test account publishes once with durable intent, final hard gates and saved remote ID/link.
2. Duplicate jobs/concurrent workers and response-loss-after-success do not create another public post; inconclusive reconciliation holds without resend.
3. Pause/cancel/shadow/quota/token/rule/revision/rights changes prevent new dispatch authorization; crashes and broker restart recover from durable state.
4. Test-account autonomy has recorded admin qualification and isolated test authorization; company-account rollout remains gated by US-043.
Demo: Show one authorized image publication, replay the job and simulate a lost response without creating another post.
Release gate: Authorized integration test; not general rollout

Title: Publish Reels and image/video Stories through the same safety gates
User story: As a admin, I want the remaining priority formats on the validated publisher, so the full core format set shares proven retry and control behavior.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Authorized real-account Reel, image-Story and video-Story sends retain platform identity, available link and attempt/reconciliation history.
2. Each format applies capability/media readiness/quotas and the same durable-intent/current-check/pause/rights rules.
3. Unsupported options and format/account failures produce actionable holds without blocking another account or format; no new bypass flow is introduced.
Demo: Show authorized Reel and image/video Story results plus a format failure isolated from another successful job.

Title: Collect available post and Story metrics with their observation windows
User story: As a operator, I want freshness-labelled metrics for published IDs, so I can distinguish actual performance from unavailable or missed data.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Available reach/impression, engagement, click and watch metrics retain published ID, value/status, provider version and observation time/window.
2. Unsupported, restricted, delayed or missing values show explicit reasons and last successful sync; they are never converted to zero.
3. Story collection follows the tested availability window for the selected API flow; missed windows and repeated sync failures are visible and alertable.
Demo: Show supported real metrics and their windows; contrast with explicit unavailable and missed-Story-window states.

Title: Read weekly reports with fair comparisons and sample sizes
User story: As a operator, I want a Persian performance report filtered by account and content dimensions, so I can compare results without mixing different post ages or hiding missing data.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Weekly/date-range reports filter by account, format, topic and posting time and show volume, top posts, period movement and sample size.
2. Comparisons use equivalent observation windows and documented calculations; incomparable/partial data is labelled or excluded with explanation.
3. Persian charts and table alternative show units, source-post links and last sync, including empty and stale-data cases.
Demo: Filter a weekly Persian report, open source posts and reproduce one equivalent-window comparison.

Title: See a concrete experiment proposal backed by actual posts
User story: As a operator, I want an explainable analytics recommendation with evidence, so I can see exactly what change is proposed and why.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The analytics role receives code-calculated comparisons and proposes one hook/duration/topic/format/slot change with a success metric.
2. Each proposal cites actual source posts, baseline/comparison, observation window and sample size; unsupported claims are rejected.
3. The UI labels insufficient evidence and does not change the calendar merely because a recommendation exists.
Demo: Open a one-variable proposal with exact posts/sample/window and show sparse evidence leaving the calendar unchanged.

Title: Schedule only qualified tests and feed bounded results back into planning
User story: As a operator, I want automatic evidence-gated calendar tests I can pause or dismiss, so learning improves planning while sparse evidence leaves the plan unchanged.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Deterministic checks enforce minimum sample/window, one-variable test policy, allowed formats, spend/posting limits and no duplicate/conflicting active test.
2. Qualified proposals enter the existing checked planner; sparse/ineligible evidence and repeated syncs create no calendar change or duplicate experiment.
3. Staff pause/dismiss is respected before future work/dispatch; measured outcomes use matched windows and can remain inconclusive.
4. Versioned bounded findings update topic/planning scores with evidence and audit, without changing prompts, hard gates or account limits.
Demo: Schedule one eligible test, replay evaluation without duplication, then pause/dismiss it and inspect bounded feedback.

Title: Qualify and enable one company account for core autonomous operation
User story: As a admin, I want an explicit evidence-based rollout decision, so the team can let all core formats run while handling exceptions.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Every required core story is accepted, including reports and analytics tests; actual platform, Persian and failure-path evidence is labelled.
2. Shadow sample/accuracy requirements pass for the account and enabled formats; critical factual/rights/sensitive/Persian failures are resolved.
3. An admin enables only the qualified company account; automatic publication requires no per-post sign-off and all pause/budget/hard gates remain active.
4. First autonomous slots are observed, operator drills pass, and unresolved conditions return the account to shadow/paused operation.
Demo: Review qualification evidence, enable one company account and observe guarded autonomous slots and exception handling.

Title: Produce and publish an image carousel after core stability
User story: As a operator, I want an ordered image carousel using existing evidence and checks, so multi-image content shares the proven production and publishing workflow.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Ordered slides use existing source/dataset/copy/rights records with editable copy, item limits and accurate previews/crops.
2. Each child and the whole revision pass checks; child/parent containers are persisted and partial preparation/ambiguous send reconcile without duplication.
3. Calendar, account limits and reports include image carousels and label unavailable aggregate/child metrics; an authorized real test succeeds.
Demo: Publish one authorized image carousel and replay a failed/uncertain parent workflow without a duplicate.

Title: Produce and publish video-only and mixed carousels
User story: As a operator, I want ordered video and mixed-media carousel support, so all Phase 1 carousel combinations use the same safe workflow.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Video-only and mixed image/video orders validate item limits, individual media readiness and actual preview/crop/timing.
2. Changing one child invalidates only its dependents and whole-carousel checks; parent publishing retains existing pause/intent/reconciliation safeguards.
3. Actual authorized tests cover both combinations, report availability is honest, and failures do not block another account/format.
Demo: Show authorized video-only and mixed carousels and a single-child correction with valid siblings reused.

Title: Accept and hand over the complete Phase 1 MVP
User story: As a product owner, I want a traceable complete release with operating ownership, so stakeholders can accept the agreed MVP and the team can maintain it.
Acceptance criteria:
1. All 16 PRD requirements and NFR/rollout obligations have accepted story evidence, including every carousel combination.
2. No critical duplicate-publication, hard-gate bypass, evidence/rights/security or Persian-quality defect remains open.
3. The delivered release has a tested restore/rollback boundary, operating runbook and named alert/budget/rotation/retention/native-review owners.
4. Known nonblocking limitations, pilot review date and stakeholder acceptance are recorded; later platforms remain outside this release.
Demo: Demonstrate complete source-to-publish-to-learning operation and hand over the accepted evidence/runbook.
